rules.description: A public comment command can become an execution API unless the actor and repository relationship are checked before any agent or write-capable step runs.
rules.remediation: Require an explicit command and allowlisted actor, team, or trusted author association before routing to the agent.
rules.title: Comment-triggered agent lacks an actor authorization gate

rules.description: Issue, pull-request, review, or comment text is attacker-controlled. Giving it to an agent that can access tools or secrets creates a prompt-injection path.
rules.remediation: Separate untrusted content from instructions, use a read-only analysis stage, validate structured output, and require approval before privileged actions.
rules.title: Untrusted event text is passed to an agent

rules.description: An agent can be manipulated or make mistakes. Combining interpretation and repository write authority removes an important control boundary.
rules.remediation: Run the agent read-only, emit a bounded proposal artifact, and apply changes in a separate reviewed job with minimal write scope.
rules.title: Agent step runs with write-capable token permissions

rules.description: Model output is untrusted data. Substituting it into a shell, eval, source, interpreter, or generated workflow turns model text into code execution.
rules.remediation: Require a typed schema, allowlisted operations, static validation, and human approval. Never execute free-form model output directly.
rules.title: Agent output is executed as code

rules.description: Direct mutation removes the independent review boundary and can amplify prompt injection or model error.
rules.remediation: Have the agent create a patch or draft pull request. Require branch protection, code review, and separate merge authority.
rules.title: Agent workflow directly pushes, merges, or mutates repository state

rules.description: Prompted agents and their dependencies may log, transmit, or accidentally disclose credentials.
rules.remediation: Keep secrets outside the reasoning context. Use a narrow broker or post-approval step that exposes only the exact operation required.
rules.title: Secret is passed directly to an agent step

rules.description: Repeated comments can create parallel agent runs, duplicate changes, race conditions, and avoidable cost.
rules.remediation: Add a stable concurrency group derived from the issue or pull request and choose an explicit cancellation policy.
rules.title: Comment-driven agent workflow has no concurrency control

rules.description: A write-capable agent job without an environment cannot use environment-level required reviewers or scoped environment secrets.
rules.remediation: Move mutation into a separate job protected by a GitHub environment with required reviewers and narrow secrets.
rules.title: Write-capable agent job has no protected environment

rules.description: A workflow without an explicit permissions block relies on repository defaults, which are harder to review and may drift.
rules.remediation: Add a top-level `permissions: contents: read` block, then grant narrower job-level write scopes only where required.
rules.title: Explicit token permissions are missing

rules.description: `write-all` grants every available GITHUB_TOKEN write scope to the workflow or job.
rules.remediation: Replace `write-all` with an explicit allowlist of the smallest required scopes.
rules.title: Write-all token permissions

rules.description: Mutable tags and branches can change after review and therefore do not provide immutable dependency identity.
rules.remediation: Pin every third-party action and reusable workflow to a full 40-character commit SHA and record the human-readable release in a comment.
rules.title: Action or reusable workflow is not pinned to a full commit SHA

rules.description: Event-controlled text embedded in a `run` or `github-script` body can change the program that the runner executes.
rules.remediation: Move the expression into an environment variable or action input and treat it strictly as data; validate it before use.
rules.title: Untrusted expression is interpolated directly into executable script

rules.description: A pull_request_target workflow can have base-repository secrets and write permissions. Checking out and executing PR-controlled code creates a pwn-request path.
rules.remediation: Use `pull_request` for untrusted build/test code. Keep pull_request_target limited to metadata-only operations and never execute PR-controlled content.
rules.title: Privileged pull_request_target workflow checks out PR-controlled code

rules.description: Self-hosted runners can retain credentials, files, network access, or state and are not guaranteed to be clean or ephemeral.
rules.remediation: Use GitHub-hosted runners for public or fork-controlled pull requests, or isolate ephemeral runners in tightly restricted groups.
rules.title: Untrusted contribution can run on a self-hosted runner

rules.description: actions/checkout persists the workflow token by default. Later tools or untrusted code in the job can reuse those credentials.
rules.remediation: Set `persist-credentials: false` and provide a narrowly scoped credential only to the exact step that needs it.
rules.title: Checkout credentials persist in a write-capable job

rules.description: Download-and-execute pipelines provide no stable identity, integrity check, or review point for remote code.
rules.remediation: Download to a file, verify a pinned digest or signature, inspect provenance, and execute only after verification.
rules.title: Network download is piped directly to a shell

rules.description: Artifacts produced by a different workflow may contain fork-controlled content. A privileged workflow must treat them as untrusted data.
rules.remediation: Bind artifacts to an expected workflow, repository, commit, and digest; parse them as data instead of executing them.
rules.title: Privileged workflow_run job executes downloaded artifacts

rules.description: Secrets in pull_request_target, issue_comment, discussion_comment, or workflow_run workflows raise the impact of prompt, script, checkout, and artifact attacks.
rules.remediation: Remove secrets from the untrusted stage. Split the workflow and use an approved environment or narrowly scoped short-lived credential in a trusted stage.
rules.title: Secrets are referenced from an externally triggerable privileged workflow

rules.description: A missing timeout allows stuck, adversarial, or unexpectedly expensive jobs to consume runner time indefinitely up to platform limits.
rules.remediation: Set a job-level timeout-minutes appropriate to the expected workload.
rules.title: Job has no timeout-minutes

rules.description: `id-token: write` allows the job to request an OIDC token. On risky triggers or without an environment boundary, the trust policy may be too broad.
rules.remediation: Issue OIDC tokens only in a trusted deployment job protected by an environment and restrictive cloud-side subject claims.
rules.title: OIDC token permission lacks a trusted deployment boundary

rules.description: A mutable container or service tag can resolve to different code after review.
rules.remediation: Pin container and service images by immutable digest, for example `image@sha256:...`.
rules.title: Container image is referenced by a mutable tag

rules.description: Allowing event-controlled text to choose runners or matrix values can redirect execution to privileged infrastructure or expand workload unexpectedly.
rules.remediation: Map untrusted input through a fixed allowlist before using it in `runs-on`, `container`, or `strategy.matrix`.
rules.title: Runner or matrix topology depends directly on untrusted input
